modelName: My PHS — EMC Value Flow · 人单合一 at Three Levels

nodes.label:
EMC Dan
Community health
cooperative's need
nodes.note:
The EMC's Dan is not a single problem — it is the health state of the entire enrolled community.

This Dan is never fully closed. It is the ongoing commitment the cooperative makes to its members: that the network of MEs, tools, and clinicians is continuously closing the distance between community need and community health.

In RenDanHeYi terms: the cooperative is not managing a population. It is in the process of becoming one with it.

nodes.label:
合
Collective problem
solving · pattern
recognition
nodes.note:
合 at the EMC level: the active merging of individual ME experiences into collective intelligence.

This is where the EMC becomes more than the sum of its MEs:
- Rare diagnoses seen once per NDC become patterns visible across the network
- A CHW in one ME discovers a better approach → SODOTO spreads it → every ME improves
- Audit conflicts that repeat across NDCs signal a systemic problem worth addressing at the cooperative level
- Physician node MEs that underperform become visible through comparative engagement scores

This is the 合 that traditional health systems cannot achieve — they have no mechanism for horizontal knowledge flow at this granularity.

nodes.label:
一
Outcomes
cost avoidance
nodes.note:
一 at the EMC level: the achieved oneness of practitioner effort and population health outcome.

Measurable signals:
- Reduction in hospitalization rate for enrolled population
- Increase in problem resolution rate (Dans closed vs. Dans open)
- Reduction in unmanaged high-stakes diagnoses surfaced by audit
- Improvement in Engagement Capacity scores across physician node MEs

These are not lagging indicators reported annually. They are live, continuously updating from the same records the tools are already generating.

nodes.label:
Cooperative
surplus
nodes.note:
Cost avoidance becomes cooperative surplus when the actuarial value of prevented events exceeds the cost of the tools and the ME network.

Surplus has three destinations:
1. Distribution back to MEs as performance pool payments
2. Reinvestment in tool infrastructure — the tools get better as the network grows
3. Member premium/cost-sharing reductions — the cooperative's members directly benefit

This is the financial argument for the model: the cooperative is not funding these tools as a cost. It is investing in a system that generates measurable return within its own actuarial boundary.

nodes.label:
ME Dan
Enrolled panel
open Dan portfolio
nodes.note:
The ME's Dan is the totality of open problems across its enrolled panel — every active problem on every person's My Health Picture.

The NDC ME can see its own Dan portfolio in aggregate:
- How many open Dans across enrolled persons
- How many are high-stakes (Urgent) vs. lower priority
- How many have an assigned physician node ME vs. unrouted
- What the Dan completion rate has been over the last 30/90 days

This is the ME's live balance sheet — not a quarterly report.

nodes.label:
合
NDC work
Dan completion
CfA closure
nodes.note:
合 at the ME level: CHWs and the persons they serve actively closing the distance between open need and resolution.

Daily work of the ME:
- Running prior diagnosis audits
- Completing My Health Picture frames before visits
- Initiating and closing physician review loops
- Facilitating My Health Choices conversations
- Earning and teaching SODOTO credentials

The ME is not a service delivery unit. It is a network of dyadic smart contracts in active motion.

nodes.label:
一
ME performance
score
nodes.note:
一 at the ME level: the aggregate oneness of the NDC's work and its panel's health movement.

The ME performance score is a composite:
- Dan completion rate (problems moved toward resolution)
- CfA closure rate (review loops opened and closed)
- SODOTO credential density (credentials earned per CHW)
- Audit completion rate
- Person engagement (health pictures current, choices documented)

This score is live, not annual. The cooperative uses it to calculate the ME's share of the performance pool.

nodes.label:
ME pool
CHW earnings
SODOTO investment
nodes.note:
The ME performance pool is the ME's share of cooperative surplus, distributed based on its performance score.

The pool has two flows:
1. Down to individual ME members — CHWs earn based on their SODOTO credentials and Dan completions; physician node MEs earn based on engagement capacity scores
2. Back into the ME's Dan portfolio — investment in tools, training slots, new SODOTO credential opportunities

The ME collectively decides how to split these flows. This is self-organization in the RenDanHeYi sense: the ME owns its economics.

nodes.label:
Individual Dan
Person's open
problem
nodes.note:
The individual Dan is the most concrete unit in the system: a specific named problem on a specific person's My Health Picture, today, with its specific evidence state and stakes.

Zhang Ruimin insisted on this concreteness deliberately. The Dan is not 'diabetes management.' It is this person's unresolved question about whether their fatigue is hypothyroidism or OSA, with three absent findings and one physician note from 2019 that has never been followed up.

That specificity is what makes 合 possible. You cannot merge with an abstraction.

nodes.label:
合
Dan closed
loop resolved
record updated
nodes.note:
合 at the individual level: the CHW and this person's open need actively closing the distance until no distance remains.

A Dan is closed when:
- The problem moves to a higher defensibility level (working hypothesis → confirmed)
- A physician review loop completes with a clinical response
- The person makes a documented choice about this problem in My Health Choices
- The problem resolves (Resolved status, dated and signed)
- The person invokes patient preference (Not pursuing — documented, dated, reversible)

Each closed Dan is a concrete instance of 人单合一 achieved.

nodes.label:
一
Value created
nodes.note:
一 at the individual level: the state of achieved oneness — the need met, the gap closed, the person and the practitioner no longer on opposite sides of a problem.

Value takes multiple forms:
- Clinical: a diagnosis confirmed, a medication adjusted, a risk identified before crisis
- Relational: the person trusts the system because they can see it working
- Financial: a hospitalization not needed, an ED visit not taken, a medication not continued without evidence
- Structural: a record that carries forward, so the next encounter begins where this one ended

nodes.label:
Individual rewards
cost-sharing ↓
CHW credential ↑
physician rate ↑
nodes.note:
Individual-level financial signals that align behavior with Dan completion:

- Person: cost-sharing reduction for current health picture, completed audit, documented choices
- CHW: SODOTO credential earnings; bonus for Dan completions above baseline
- Physician node ME: differential reimbursement based on engagement capacity score; bonus for response completeness

None of these require separate reporting infrastructure. The cooperative reads the same records the tools are already generating.

nodes.label:
Tool investment
infrastructure
improves
nodes.note:
A portion of cooperative surplus flows into tool infrastructure — the coupler frames, the SCP plugins, the audit scoring algorithms, the graph diagrams themselves.

This creates a feedback loop that traditional healthcare cannot replicate: as the network grows and closes more Dans, it generates more surplus, which improves the tools, which enables more precise Dan identification and closure, which generates more surplus.

The tools are not a cost center. They are a compounding investment.

nodes.label:
Peer effects
person ↔ person
ME ↔ ME
nodes.note:
Peer effects operate at both levels simultaneously and are among the most powerful forces in the system.

Person-to-person: an enrolled neighbor who visibly navigates a complex diagnosis well is a more persuasive signal than any public health campaign. The cooperative can amplify this deliberately through peer health circles and patient SODOTO credentials.

ME-to-ME: comparative performance data across NDC MEs creates implicit professional norms. High-performing MEs attract enrollment, retain CHWs, and become SODOTO teaching nodes for the network.

Peer effects are not designed — they emerge from transparency. Making Dan completion rates visible across the EMC is sufficient.

nodes.label:
SODOTO
Teach One
credential flow
nodes.note:
SODOTO (See One, Do One, Teach One) is the mechanism by which individual Dan competency becomes EMC collective competency.

The Teach One phase is the critical transmission:
- A CHW who has closed 10 audit Dans teaches a peer → earns a master credential → earns more
- The peer who learns has done so from someone with proven practice, not a manual
- The EMC's collective credential density grows without top-down training investment

Every credential earned is evidence of a Dan closed. Every Teach One event is a peer effect deliberately structured into the incentive system.

nodes.label:
人单合一
Rén — practitioner
Dān — specific need
合 — the merging
一 — oneness achieved
nodes.note:
人单合一 is not 'person-order-integration.' It is:

The person (人) and the order (单) are in the active process (合) of becoming one (一).

合 and 一 are not a compound meaning 'unity.' 合 is what is happening — the merging. 一 is what is being arrived at — oneness. The phrase describes a dynamic, not a state.

At every level of this diagram — individual, ME, EMC — the same movement is occurring: the practitioner and the need are continuously closing the distance between themselves until no distance remains.

The CHW's daily work IS the Dan, not a response to it. That is the philosophical weight Zhang Ruimin was carrying, and it is exactly the condition these tools are designed to create.
